methodology.observation_window_basis: Window starts at the latest successful immutable run's window_end and ends at the scheduled observation cutoff for the October 6 weekday occurrence.
methodology.ranking_basis: Signal strength rather than popularity, emphasizing commercialization, deployment, manufacturing capacity, infrastructure, strategic partnerships, regulatory approval, and meaningful technical milestones.
methodology.source_policy: Prefer primary company, government, regulatory, and research-institution sources.
methodology.repeat_policy: Recent immutable findings and event identities were checked; repeated events are included only for material updates with preserved event_key and material_update_from.
excluded_noise: market-price movement without underlying technical or commercial change

provenance.source: Scheduled weekday Technology Trend Update using live public-source research and the immutable GitHub ledger.
provenance.notes: Publication-request branch handoff; legacy history and longitudinal visual were not used.

findings.headline: Google and Constellation agree to unlock 890 MW of new nuclear capacity across six operating plants
findings.summary: Google and Constellation announced a long-term collaboration financing physical and digital upgrades at six nuclear plants in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, expected to add 890 MW of clean baseload capacity to the PJM grid. Google will also provide Gemini Enterprise technology for nuclear-plant operations.
findings.why_it_matters: This couples hyperscale data-center demand directly to expansion of existing nuclear generation, converting AI-driven load growth into financed grid capacity rather than relying only on new-build generation.
findings.trend_statement: AI infrastructure demand is becoming a direct financing mechanism for uprating existing firm-power assets and modernizing grid operations.

source_links.title: Why we're backing America's existing nuclear plants

findings.headline: Xanadu moves photonic quantum components from lab-scale prototyping toward 300 mm industrial production with GlobalFoundries
findings.summary: Xanadu and GlobalFoundries announced a multi-year partnership to transfer ultra-low-loss silicon nitride photonics and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors onto GF's 300 mm manufacturing line in Malta, New York. The output is intended to support Xanadu's fault-tolerant demonstrators and future quantum data centers.
findings.why_it_matters: Quantum-computing progress increasingly depends on repeatable semiconductor-scale manufacturing, and this agreement establishes a concrete industrialization path for two critical photonic components.
findings.trend_statement: Quantum hardware is beginning to cross from bespoke laboratory fabrication into conventional high-volume semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure.

source_links.title: Xanadu and GlobalFoundries Announce Strategic Partnership to Accelerate Utility-Scale Quantum Manufacturing

findings.headline: Type One Energy raises $200 million to industrialize its stellarator fusion power-plant program
findings.summary: Type One Energy completed a $200 million Series B co-led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Clutterbuck Capital, with Siemens Energy Ventures and others participating. The company says the financing advances Project Infinity and its partner-based strategy for commercial fusion following the project's initial operating license.
findings.why_it_matters: The financing adds substantial private and strategic-industrial capital behind a licensed engineering path intended to move stellarator fusion from physics validation toward a deployable power-plant design.
findings.trend_statement: Fusion commercialization is attracting larger industrially connected financing rounds focused on engineering prototypes and manufacturable power plants rather than basic plasma research alone.

source_links.title: Type One Energy Completes $200M Series B Financing
